instructions: Human-reviewed losses/REQs. Wording tightened to world-level REQs.

values: privacy of their own driving record

goals.text: Keep the dashcam useful as accident evidence without turning the car into a public search node
Avoid surprise cost, crash risk, or legal blowback from ChildFind

items.loss: The owner's everyday driving video and face embeddings are retained or reused after an authorized search ends.
items.req: After an authorized search expires, people and vehicles recorded by the owner's dashcam are not identifiable from anything retained for ChildFind.
items.harm_note: Primary product promise of the dashcam is private evidence, not a biometric database.

items.loss: The owner receives an unexpected cellular bill because ChildFind uploaded video through their phone.
items.req: The owner is not billed for cellular data used by ChildFind beyond a limit they accepted in advance.
items.harm_note: Data-charge fear is named in the scenario and will drive silent opt-out.

items.loss: A ChildFind match notification distracts the driver and contributes to a crash.
items.req: While the vehicle is moving, the driver is not prompted to inspect a possible-match image.
items.harm_note: Driving safety dominates child-search UX; a crash makes the feature indefensible to OEMs.

items.loss: After a child is found near the owner's route, the owner is blamed or sued for not reporting.
items.req: An owner who had the device powered and enrolled is not treated as having a personal duty to have noticed the child.
items.harm_note: Legal duty-to-rescue confusion will chill adoption.

items.loss: Always-on matching drains the battery or fills storage so the dashcam is dead when a crash happens.
items.req: The dashcam continues to record a crash loop even when a ChildFind search is active.
items.harm_note: The product's original job is crash evidence; cannibalizing it is an organizational own-goal.

items.loss: Someone uses a fake 'missing child' enrollment to reconstruct the owner's routine from sighting metadata.
items.req: A person who is not the subject of a bona fide, authority-backed search cannot obtain a trail of where the owner's car has been.
items.harm_note: The search channel is a location oracle if authorization is weak.

goals.text: Be found while still in the area where a participating camera saw them
Not be further harmed by how the search is conducted or publicized

items.loss: The child remains missing even though they walked through a participating camera's view.
items.req: If a missing child is physically visible in the field of view of a participating dashcam during an authorized search, the coordinating law-enforcement unit learns of that co-location while the child is still in the same local area.
items.harm_note: This is the core mission requirement; it depends on the ML model and on radios the dashcam does not have.

items.loss: A public or in-app alert warns an abductor, who relocates the child before officers arrive.
items.req: An abductor traveling with the child does not receive a real-time notice that a nearby camera just matched the child.
items.harm_note: Faster reports help authorities only if they are not also faster reports to the offender.

items.loss: The recovered child is filmed, identified, and the still circulates on social media.
items.req: After recovery, the child's face from ChildFind stills is not available to the general public.
items.harm_note: Rescue can become a second victimization.

items.loss: Search resources chase a lookalike while the actual child is moved elsewhere.
items.req: A false sighting does not cause the only available officers in the true vicinity to leave that vicinity.
items.harm_note: False positives are not a victimless precision metric; they steal time from the child.

items.loss: The child is in view but disguised or too young for an adult-tuned face model, so no one looks at the frame.
items.req: A missing young child who is visibly present and unoccluded in a participating camera's view is not overlooked solely because they are a small child rather than an adult.
items.harm_note: Contractor expertise in distorted/low-light adult faces is the wrong domain.

items.loss: The child's last known location is published so precisely that a dangerous guardian finds them first.
items.req: A person who is a threat to the child does not obtain a live, meter-accurate location from ChildFind.
items.harm_note: Custody and domestic-violence cases are common in missing-child reports.

goals.text: Get timely, truthful information that helps recover the child
Not have the family's other children or address exposed by the search

items.loss: Parents are told of 'possible sightings' that are not their child, then crash emotionally and stop trusting later true reports.
items.req: Parents are not notified of a sighting unless the coordinating unit has judged it worth acting on.
items.harm_note: Unfiltered model output is not a family communication channel.

items.loss: A real nearby sighting sits in a queue while parents are told 'no new information'.
items.req: When a sighting is judged actionable, the parents (or their designated liaison) hear about it before the information is stale.
items.harm_note: Delay is a different failure from silence after a miss.

items.loss: The search packet includes a home address and photos of siblings that then leak.
items.req: Home address and images of children who are not the missing child do not leave the coordinating unit's custody.
items.harm_note: Search packets are over-broad because intake copies the whole case file.

items.loss: A sibling or the searching parent is matched as the 'abductor' or as the child and is detained.
items.req: Family members who are with the missing child's siblings in public are not detained solely because a ChildFind score fired on a related face.
items.harm_note: Related faces are a known failure mode of face systems.

items.loss: The search is quietly ended because the non-profit is flooded, and parents are not told the network is no longer looking.
items.req: Parents know whether participating cameras are still being asked to search for their child.
items.harm_note: Operational degradation must be visible to the people who think a net is out there.

goals.text: Receive sightings that are timely, located, and worth sending a unit
Not create an unlawful or indefensible search record

items.loss: Dispatch burns a shift on false pins and has no unit left for a later true pin.
items.req: A ChildFind notice does not cause officers to abandon a higher-priority last-known area without a human decision.
items.harm_note: The model must not be allowed to steer cars by itself.

items.loss: A true sighting arrives hours later, after the child has left the area.
items.req: When a participating camera had the child in view, dispatch has the notice while a search of that area can still succeed.
items.harm_note: Connectivity, not just accuracy, sets whether 'faster is more useful' is true.

items.loss: A stop or search based on ChildFind is thrown out, and the case is damaged.
items.req: Officers acting on a ChildFind notice can show a lawful, purpose-limited, time-bounded authorization for that search-id.
items.harm_note: Legal details are unsettled; the machine must still leave a paper trail.

items.loss: The same pipeline is reused for shoplifting, immigration, or protest monitoring.
items.req: Person matching on consumer dashcams is not applied to a purpose other than an authorized missing-child search.
items.harm_note: Once the camera network exists, other agencies will ask.

items.loss: Operators ignore the inbox because yesterday it was 400 low-quality stills.
items.req: The coordinating unit's ChildFind inbox remains usable on a typical search day (on the order of the national Amber rate, not a continuous firehose).
items.harm_note: Human attention is part of the environment the REQ depends on.

items.loss: Traditional canvassing stops because 'the cameras would have seen them'.
items.req: Investigators continue non-camera search activity even while ChildFind is active.
items.harm_note: Automation complacency is an environmental/organizational failure.

goals.text: Increase recoveries without becoming a surveillance brand
Keep volunteers and donors engaged

items.loss: A privacy scandal ends the partnership and the search capability with it.
items.req: Bystanders and families do not experience a ChildFind privacy incident that becomes public during the partnership.
items.harm_note: Trust is the non-profit's actual capital.

items.loss: Donors leave after a high-profile miss that is blamed on the non-profit 'using AI'.
items.req: The public description of a miss does not claim that cameras covered a place they did not.
items.harm_note: Overclaiming coverage is how AI partnerships die.

items.loss: Volunteer reviewers quit because the queue is mostly not-the-child stills.
items.req: Volunteer review load stays within a published per-search budget the non-profit accepted.
items.harm_note: Human review is a mitigation for model errors; it can become the new hazard.

items.loss: The company uses the non-profit's name to sell dashcams, then ships a weaker privacy mode than the partnership described.
items.req: Devices advertised under the partnership actually run the same matching and retention rules the non-profit signed.
items.harm_note: SKU fragmentation is how ethics agreements die.

items.loss: Search photos of children circulate in volunteer Slack, press, or the contractor's demo reel.
items.req: A child's search photo is not available to people outside the authorized search roles.
items.harm_note: Distribution, not collection, is where most leaks happen.

goals.text: Offer ChildFind as a differentiator without creating a recall
Not be seen as shipping a mass-surveillance car

items.loss: A crash is attributed to a ChildFind prompt or to compute starving the vehicle electrical system.
items.req: ChildFind does not present driving-relevant alerts to the driver and does not take the vehicle electrical system below the OEM's reserved budget.
items.harm_note: NHTSA will not care that the ML model was accurate.

items.loss: Press describes the car as a rolling face-recognition network; OEM cancels the SKU.
items.req: Uninvolved people photographed by the car are not identified by name or persistent id as part of ChildFind.
items.harm_note: OEM brand risk is mostly about bystanders, not about missing children.

items.loss: Warranty returns spike because ChildFind overheats or bricks low-end units.
items.req: Low-end hardware either performs matching within thermal limits or reports itself as non-participating rather than failing.
items.harm_note: Heterogeneous compute is in the scenario.

items.loss: A regulator treats always-on interior/cabin matching as illegal surveillance in the car.
items.req: Cabin-facing cameras, if present, are not used to match passengers for ChildFind.
items.harm_note: Many 'dashcams' are dual-channel.

items.loss: Dealers cannot explain the feature, so they disable it, leaving advertised coverage fictional.
items.req: A car advertised as ChildFind-capable is actually enrolled or is labeled at sale as not enrolled.
items.harm_note: Channel fiction shows up as empty density maps.

goals.text: Deliver a usable person-recognition stack without absorbing the manufacturer's product risk
Keep training data and weights from leaking via on-device deployment

items.loss: On-device weights are extracted from a consumer dashcam and republished.
items.req: A person who buys a dashcam does not obtain a working copy of the contractor's production model weights.
items.harm_note: Offline deployment is explicitly on the table in the scenario.

items.loss: Public audits show large error gaps on children or on darker skin, and the contractor is named.
items.req: Disparities in whether a visible missing child is reported are not systematically associated with the child's age band or skin tone in deployed searches.
items.harm_note: This is a world-level fairness requirement, not 'equal F1 on a benchmark'.

items.loss: Latency or downtime of a cloud Rekognition-like path misses the useful window.
items.req: A sighting is not lost solely because a cloud inference endpoint was slow or unreachable.
items.harm_note: The dashcam is already offline; adding a cloud round-trip stacks two radios.

items.loss: Fine-tuning uses photos the contractor had no license to train on, and a lawsuit lands on both companies.
items.req: A child's photo provided for a live search is not used to train or advertise a model.
items.harm_note: Live searches are the most sensitive data the contractor will ever see.

items.loss: The contractor is subpoenaed as the 'face recognition company' for every ChildFind case.
items.req: The contractor does not receive a copy of every production video frame, only what the manufacturer must send to meet a specified inference path.
items.harm_note: Data minimization is also liability minimization.

goals.text: Move through streets without being biometrically identified by a consumer camera network
Not have an image from a sensitive place reused later

items.loss: A bystander's face is embedded and kept so they can be re-identified after the search ends.
items.req: A person who is not the subject of an authorized search is not assigned a persistent identity from ChildFind processing.
items.harm_note: This is the mass-surveillance requirement hiding inside a child-safety feature.

items.loss: A still of a bystander at a clinic, shelter, or protest is later reused in another investigation.
items.req: ChildFind stills are not available to reuse for a purpose other than the originating missing-child search.
items.harm_note: Secondary use is how dashcams become police databases.

items.loss: People avoid streets, schools, or clinics known to be dense with enrolled cars.
items.req: The public is not given a live map of which cars are currently matching faces.
items.harm_note: Transparency can itself become a chilling-effect channel.

items.loss: A child bystander's face is enrolled into a gallery 'to improve child recall' without a parent.
items.req: Children who are not the missing child are not added to any biometric gallery from dashcam footage.
items.harm_note: The obvious ML fix (more child faces) is itself a harm.

items.loss: An employer, landlord, or immigration officer obtains a still showing where a bystander was.
items.req: A ChildFind still of a bystander is not obtainable by a private party who wants to know where that person was.
items.harm_note: The threat is not only the state.

items.loss: A bystander is stopped because they were next to a possible match in the same frame.
items.req: Presence in the same video frame as a possible match does not by itself cause a bystander to be treated as a suspect companion.
items.harm_note: Association is a world harm the model does not even 'predict' explicitly.

goals.text: Go about daily life without being treated as the missing child or their abductor
Have a way to end a false identification quickly

items.loss: Police stop a lookalike child in public based on a ChildFind pin.
items.req: A child who is not the missing child is not stopped by police solely because a dashcam produced a possible-match notice.
items.harm_note: False-positive harm is the one developers underweight when they optimize recall.

items.loss: The caregiver is arrested as an abductor because they are walking with a lookalike.
items.req: An adult accompanying a child who is not missing is not arrested solely on a ChildFind possible-match.
items.harm_note: The 'abductor' inference is a world action with no supporting SPEC unless we invent one.

items.loss: A school or store goes into lockdown because a public app showed a nearby match.
items.req: Schools and businesses do not receive automated ChildFind match alerts about children on their premises.
items.harm_note: The blast radius of a FP includes institutions.

items.loss: A lookalike's photo remains associated with the case online after the true child is found.
items.req: Once a possible-match is judged to be the wrong child, that still is not kept as part of a public or family-visible case story.
items.harm_note: Correction has to be as operational as detection.

items.loss: The lookalike child becomes afraid of cameras and of going outside.
items.req: A mistaken ChildFind contact is followed by a clear, child-appropriate explanation that they are not in trouble and were not the missing child.
items.harm_note: Dignity after a FP is a world requirement on operators, not on the model.

goals.text: Biometric processing of the public has a legal basis, limits, and a way to challenge it
Children's data is treated as a special category, not as 'just another face'

items.loss: The network performs biometric processing of the general public without a valid legal basis.
items.req: Faces of people who are not the search subject are not biometrically processed except as a transient comparison during an authorized, time-bounded search.
items.harm_note: If this REQ fails, the feature is illegal even when it finds children.

items.loss: Children's images move across borders to a contractor region without safeguards.
items.req: A child's search photo and any matching still remain in the jurisdiction the case was opened in, unless a recorded transfer mechanism applies.
items.harm_note: Rekognition-like infrastructure is often multi-region by default.

items.loss: Accident-evidence recordings are silently joined to a police biometric store.
items.req: Crash-loop recordings made for accident evidence are not searchable as a biometric database.
items.harm_note: Purpose limitation between the two product jobs.

items.loss: A subject cannot find out whether they were matched, or get deletion, because the system is opaque.
items.req: A person who was the subject of a ChildFind still can have that still deleted through a defined request path once the search has closed, and can learn whether a still existed.
items.harm_note: Opaque ML systems fail access/deletion rights.

items.loss: A precedent is set that any emotional child-safety story justifies biometric scanning of a city.
items.req: Each search remains individually authorized, time-bounded, and geographically bounded rather than becoming a standing scan of all enrolled cameras.
items.harm_note: The 1-alert/day statistic is a design gift; ignore it and you get always-on scanning.

goals.text: Host an edge drop-off without becoming a police checkpoint
Not pay unbounded bandwidth or eat a lawsuit

items.loss: Customers treat the station as a surveillance site and stop coming.
items.req: Drivers using the station are not shown, and do not have to pass, a face-matching checkpoint to buy fuel.
items.harm_note: Edge computing excitement in the scenario is a product risk, not a free lunch.

items.loss: A child was at the pump and not reported; the station is sued for hosting the system.
items.req: Hosting an offload kiosk is not treated as a promise that everyone on the forecourt will be matched.
items.harm_note: Coverage fiction again, now at a place.

items.loss: Someone uses the kiosk network to pull faces of all customers.
items.req: The partner network cannot be queried for people who did not just offload an enrolled dashcam queue.
items.harm_note: A new shared phenomenon (the kiosk) is a new attack surface.

items.loss: The kiosk is stolen or smashed and stored blobs are taken.
items.req: Theft of a kiosk does not disclose identifiable stills or search photos.
items.harm_note: Physical security of edge is not like cloud security.

items.loss: Bandwidth bills from video offload exceed the partnership's value.
items.req: The partner is not asked to carry raw video, only small encrypted reports within a contracted byte budget.
items.harm_note: If the design needs full video at the edge, the partnership dies or becomes extractive.

values: not being punished for opting out

goals.text: Keep driving for a living without turning passengers into search subjects
Not be deactivated for refusing ChildFind

items.loss: A passenger is matched or still-captured without knowing a search was running in the car they hired.
items.req: A rideshare passenger is not biometrically compared to a missing-child photo unless they have been told a search is active in that vehicle and can decline the ride.
items.harm_note: Employment dashcams break the consumer opt-in story.

items.loss: The driver is deactivated or loses a bonus for turning ChildFind off.
items.req: A driver who disables ChildFind does not automatically lose the ability to work.
items.harm_note: Otherwise 'opt-in' is fiction.

items.loss: A passenger gives a one-star review because a match prompt or LED made them feel watched.
items.req: Passengers are not shown missing-child photos or match stills during a trip.
items.harm_note: UX meant for volunteer drivers is wrong in a taxi.

items.loss: Footage of a fare dispute is pulled because it happened to be in a ChildFind queue.
items.req: A passenger–driver dispute is not investigated through ChildFind stills collected for a missing-child search.
items.harm_note: Secondary use inside the same car.

items.loss: The driver's personal phone plan is billed for fleet matching uploads.
items.req: Cellular bytes used for ChildFind on a fleet vehicle are not charged to the driver's personal plan without their agreement.
items.harm_note: Same data-cost REQ as S01, but the payer is different.
